Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently gave a talk at the Startup School 2026 event, and the video of her presentation has been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel. You can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared wonderful stories and design wisdom

It has been over 40 years since the original Macintosh was released, yet the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still look just as eye-catching today as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh remain part of macOS to this day, preserved both in spirit and in their original form. From the Command key symbol and the Happy Mac startup icon to system fonts and the hand-shaped cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

While anyone who has studied Apple's history may have seen Kare's sketches, or even read or listened to her interviews discussing that early work, it's still fascinating to hear her recount firsthand the passion and frustrations she felt back when graphical user interfaces and bitmap images were still uncharted territory.

So, if you're interested in design, fascinated by Apple's history, or simply enjoy hearing someone share a lifelong passion from a professional perspective, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also discussed how she joined the company, showcased her work after leaving, shared some early Apple anecdotes, and quoted other legendary designers, bringing additional inspiration to the audience.
